courses.title: Transport Phenomena (ChBE 3200, Undergraduate)
paragraphs: I served as the graduate teaching assistant for the Undergraduate Transport Phenomena course in Fall 2023. My primary duty was to conduct recitation problem-solving sessions and office hours, and grade and advise students on the course project.

I was lucky enough to take two regular lectures in the course on "Macroscopic Energy Balance and Bernoulli Principle" (Slides are available here: [Lecture 1](/Teaching/GT/UG_TP_Slides/Lecture8_09_08_2023.pptx) and [Lecture 2](/Teaching/GT/UG_TP_Slides/Lecture9_09_11_2023.pptx)). I had won the "Shell Outstanding Teaching Assistant Award" for teaching this course but the real reward was the student comments I had received at the end of the course in feedback survey. Here are some of the excerpts:
testimonials: Fantastic at explaining problems and helping students get to the solution by learning rather than copying
Sayan was absolutely phenomenal at explaining concepts. There were several points in the class where I was very confused and when I would ask him for an explanation it would make perfect sense. ....
The TA was excellent at explaining concepts in an approachable and easy-to-understand manner
Phenomenal TA and should be allowed to teach the class full time.
Exceptional teaching skills and knowledge of content. Was able to answer pretty much any question anyone asked him
Single handedly the greatest TA I ever had.
Great screencasts and reviews for exams.

courses.title: Data Analytics for Chemical Engineers (ChBE 4745/6745)
paragraphs: The primary objective of this course was to introduce data science and machine learning techniques for analyzing, interpreting, and visualizing datasets commonly encountered in chemical and biomolecular engineering. The course was aimed at undergraduate seniors and graduate students.

I was a TA for this course, taught by my PhD advisor Dr. A. J. Medford in Fall 2025. When I was a student in this course in Fall 2024, Dr. Medford piloted a new format of final examination - "Write your own problem (WYOP)" in response to improving Large Language Models and chatbots for coding tasks. I returned in the subsequent Fall as a Teaching Assistant and helped develop the pattern and rubric more rigorously for WYOP. All the exams - midterm and final - were replaced with WYOP-style exams.

Georgia Tech released [The Georgia Tech Academic AI Playbook: 2026 Edition](https://sites.gatech.edu/academic-ai-playbook/) - a cool resource pooled across the institute documenting how the faculty reacted to AI in teaching & research. You can read more about our contribution regarding the [WYOP approach](https://c14750.wpmucdn.com/5843/files/2026/09/gt-ai-playbook-2026-241-244-medford-yu-bhowmik-replacing-exams-with-write.pdf) in the 2026 edition of the playbook.

My other responsibilities included conducting office hours and advising students on the course-long project. I had won the "Best Online TA Award" for the department from the Center for Teaching and Learning, GT and was recognized in the institute-wide ceremony. As always, my real reward was the student feedback at the end of the course where a student remarked, "Sayan was an absolute beast; he was super helpful and responsive when I had questions for him" and would "buy him a beer if I saw him out on a weekend," while another student "truly valued the Python session at the beginning of the semester".

paragraphs: Following contains the pre-recorded lectures which were used for the Vertically Integrated Projects: Big Data and Quantum Mechanics class. The lectures on DFT were recorded in the year 2024 when I served as the instructor for the first time in this course. I have taught this course in different capacities including subteam lead from 2024 - 2027 in the Fall and Spring semesters. Dr. A. J. Medford has been running this course with his graduate students and postdocs serving as instructors at Georgia Tech since 2017. More can be found about this course at [VIP-BDQM](https://www.medford.chbe.gatech.edu/training-materials/docs/VIP_syllabus.html#).
Students ranged from Undergraduate research students to graduate students in various online MS programs run at GT.
